unspecified.behavior: On the search page, a held failed, tooLarge or refused notice for an in: key disappears while the query is impossible and reappears unchanged, with no new resolution, when the contradiction is removed.

scores.reason: Typing then deleting a contradicting token on a refused '-in:' query briefly shows the empty state, then the same notice again; this is consistent with the spec but not described.

After an in: name fails, is too large or is refused, the user makes the query impossible and then undoes that edit; the same notice comes back with no new resolution (useFolderFiles.ts:302 keeps the held resolution, and :355 only hides it while impossible). The notice is still accurate for that key, and 再試行 stays available.

unspecified.behavior: A -in: name that no collection of the drive carries (a typo) is sent as exclude_collection and silently excludes nothing.

scores.reason: Typing '-in:Tirp' shows an Exclude chip over unfiltered results, so the user may believe the collection was excluded.

If the user mistypes a collection name after -in:, it goes out as exclude_collection (useFolderFiles.ts:392-393), excludes nothing, and the results look like an unfiltered list, though the chip still shows the mistyped name.

scores.reason: After editing an in: query through a contradiction and back, the page may for one render show the reset listing's empty state or a 0 count before loading starts, instead of the pending state the in: gate normally gives.

unspecified.behavior: A held failed, tooLarge or refused notice for an in: key reappears, without resolving again, when an intervening impossible edit is undone.

scores.reason: Removing the contradicting token brings back the same notice as before; only 再試行 or a key change resolves again, as I28 asks.

Same behavior as claude-read index 0: undoing an impossible edit brings back the held failed, tooLarge or refused notice for an unchanged in: key without resolving again. This matches the documented rule that only a key change, 再試行 or a reload resolves again.
